title: Small but mighty, this has become my favorite Staub!
text:
Small but mighty, this has become my favorite Staub!. I own a number of Staub cocottes in various shapes and sizes including the pumpkin, tomato, and oval, so when I heard that Staub had come out with a rice cooker modeled on the Japanese hagama that can cook rice in only 20 minutes, I was intrigued.

I've used a Zojirushi rice cooker for the last seven years, but it takes an hour to make even one cup of white rice, so I loved the idea of a stovetop rice cooker that only takes 10 minutes of active cooking time (plus steaming and soaking).

I tested out the petite French oven making white (sushi) rice, the tomato risotto recipe from Staub Japan's site, and the bacon and mushroom rice. First, rinse and soak your rice for 30 minutes. Next, add the rice and fresh water to the cocotte. Bring to a rapid boil (until small bubbles come up around the edges). Stir everything well, cover, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to steam for 10-15 minutes (longer steaming equals fluffier rice!).

Rice comes out perfectly every time and the petite French oven makes an attractive serving dish as well. I have several petite ovens in different colors including sapphire and la mer, and they are also fantastic for dips, soups, fondues and anytime you don't feel like hauling out a larger pot. It's great for dinners for one or two or reheating leftovers too!

description: Staub's 1. 5 quart Cast Iron Petite French Oven boasts the benefits of a full-size cocotte in a compact size. Get fluffy rice, tender grains and creamy oatmeal thanks to Staub's signature new lid. Staub's latest innovation, the Chistera drop-structure lid, has solved the challenge of curved lids - they limit moisture to sides - by ensuring continuous condensation throughout. Unlike countertop rice cookers, Staub's Petite French Oven can be transported from the stovetop to the table. No need for serving bowls; these charming cocottes take care of both cooking and plating. Rice has never been so easy to make.
